faqs.a: No, a GIC is not mandatory on the regular stream. IRCC accepts bank statements, education loans, scholarship letters, tuition payment receipts and sponsor letters. A GIC of 23,448 dollars or more from a participating Canadian bank remains one of the cleanest and most trusted forms of proof, however.

headline: Canada Study Permit 2026: Requirements, Funds and Application Steps
metaDescription: Canada study permit 2026: CAD 23,448 living-cost proof of funds, acceptance letter, PAL rules, master's and PhD exemptions and application steps.

sections.content:
A Canadian study permit application rests on three pillars: a letter of acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution, proof that you can pay for tuition and living costs, and a credible study plan. Undergraduate and college students also need a Provincial Attestation Letter from the province.

IRCC officers assess not just the amount of money but its source. Six months of clean bank statements with a clear paper trail beat a sudden large deposit. Language ability, ties to your home country and a convincing rationale for the chosen program all feed into the decision.
sections.title: What a Study Permit Application Needs

sections.content:
For applications submitted on or after 1 September 2026, a single applicant outside Quebec must demonstrate at least CAD 23,448 in first-year living costs, on top of tuition and travel. The amount rises with family size: 29,192 dollars for two people, 35,888 for three and 43,572 for four.

Accepted proof includes bank statements, a Guaranteed Investment Certificate of 23,448 dollars or more from a participating Canadian bank, education loans, scholarship award letters, tuition payment receipts and signed sponsor letters. Quebec follows a different process through the CAQ, assessed by Quebec's immigration ministry.
sections.title: Proof of Funds: Amounts and Accepted Documents

sections.content:
From 1 January 2026, master's and PhD students at public Canadian universities are exempt from the national study permit cap and from the Provincial Attestation Letter requirement. PhD applicants from outside Canada can see permits processed in as little as 14 days.

The exemption applies only to degree-granting programs at public institutions. Graduate diplomas, certificates and programs at private colleges still need a PAL and count against the cap, so check your institution's status before relying on the exemption.
sections.title: Master's and PhD Exemptions

sections.content:
Secure admission and your letter of acceptance first, then obtain the Provincial Attestation Letter if your program requires one. Gather financial documents covering the last four to six months and make sure every deposit is explained.

Apply online through the IRCC portal with biometrics, and in most cases a medical exam. Processing times vary by country, so apply as early as possible: a strong, complete application is essential, since poorly documented funds are one of the most common reasons for refusal.
